title: Three-dimensional Biomimetic Technology: Novel Biorubber Creates Defined Micro- and Macro-scale Architectures in Collagen Hydrogels
protocol: Extract collagen following a previously published procedure.
Thaw a minimum of 20 ml of collagen.
Cut three pieces of aluminum foil (about 6 x 6 cm) and shape each one as a pan using the bottom of a 25 ml beaker.
Record the weight of each shaped aluminum pan.
Add approximately 0.5 - 0.8 g of collagen to each aluminum pan.
Record the total weight of each aluminum pan with added collagen.
Calculate the weight of the collagen in each pan: Collagen weight = Pan and collagen weight - Pan weight.
Place the three aluminum pans containing collagen into an oven at 100 °C for 24 hours.
After 24 hours, remove the pans from the oven and record their weights.
Record the weight of each aluminum pan with dehydrated collagen.
Calculate the weight of the dehydrated collagen: Dehydrated collagen weight = Pan and dehydrated collagen weight - Pan weight.
Calculate the percentage of solid for the three samples to determine the collagen solid concentration.
Calculate the average collagen solid content of the batch.
Adjust the pH of the collagen batch to 3 using small amounts of 12 N Hydrochloric Acid (HCl).
Add HCl to the side of the tube and stir with a spatula to mix with the collagen.
Keep the mixture on ice at all times during pH adjustment.
Let the collagen sit overnight at 4 °C after reaching pH 3.
Prepare 0.02 M PBS solution by adding two PBS tablets to 100 ml of water.
Create a 30% BSA solution using 2x PBS and Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA).
Add one-third of the 2x PBS (e.g., 10 ml) to a flask with a stir bar.
Add half of the required BSA (e.g., 6.45 g BSA) to the flask.
Wet the dry BSA solute using a spatula and mix thoroughly.
Clean stainless steel molds using sonicator at a frequency of 35 kHz.
Submerge the molds in water and ice during sonication.
Run the sonicator for two periods of 90 min each while keeping the molds cold.
Use a needle to ensure there is no material in the Luer lock stainless steel or brass connector.
Clean the entire surface of the two sides of the molds with soap and water.
Verify that there is no obstruction in the channels.
Place the molds, screws, and Luer lock connector in an autoclave bag and autoclave them.
Fill a bottle half way with commercially available lard (mixed fatty acid release agent).
Replace the cap with a regular cap bottle.
Place the bottle in an autoclave bag and autoclave it.
Warm up the lard for 45 sec or until clear and liquid in a microwave.
Screw the air sprayer lid to the lard bottle.
Connect the lid with the sprayer.
Attach the sprayer to the air source at the lab bench.
Open the air valve, and open the nozzle of the sprayer until it starts wetting the surface of a paper towel.
Spray lard perpendicular to the mold surface until fully covered.
Place each sprayed piece in a Petri dish and seal it.
Store molds at 4 °C for 2 hr.
Sterilize the molds by exposing them to UV light for 30 min.
Place the molds back at 4 °C until ready for reaction injection.
Sterilize all mixing components by exposing them to UV light for 30 min in the PCR hood.
Place the tip cap on the solution holder.
Add 30% BSA to one chamber of the double syringe, leaving space for an O ring.
Add 3% glutaraldehyde solution to the other chamber of the double syringe, leaving space for an O ring.
Place the double syringe on the dispenser.
Replace the cap with the mixing tip.
Screw the two stainless steel mold pieces together.
Hold the dispenser in the upright position and quickly squeeze the handle one time to release a small amount of BSA mixed with glutaraldehyde.
Attach the stainless steel Y mold's Luer lock connector to the syringe tip quickly after releasing the air.
Cover each exhaust of the outflow channels by pressing them to the sides of the autoclave bag to fill inside voids with solution.
Place molds horizontally and inject again.
Detach the molds from dispenser and place in a 25 mm Petri dish.
Wrap Parafilm around the Petri dish to prevent dehydration of the rubber.
Place the mold in the 4°C fridge overnight.
Adjust the collagen concentration using the percentage of collagen solids.
Make 10 ml of 1.75% collagen by adjusting initial collagen concentration with cold water.
Use a calibrated pH meter to adjust the pH to 3 using 12 N Hydrochloric Acid, adding acid to the side of the tube.
Stir the mixture quickly after pushing the acid into the collagen.
Weigh 4 g of collagen in a separate conical tube.
Centrifuge the collagen at 4°C and 9,343 x g for 20-30 min to remove air.
Turn on the UV light of the tissue culture hood for 30 min to sterilize the hood.
Sterilize forceps, spatula, and scalpel by autoclaving.
Mix 14 µl of laminin with 4 ml of collagen to achieve a final concentration of 10 µg/µl laminin.
Gamma irradiate the collagen for 8.6 min to reach 1,200 cGy.
Make a 0.2 N HEPES solution in water and adjust its pH to 9 using small amounts of 1-5 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
Mix 1.5 ml of 0.2 N HEPES (pH 9) with 1.5 ml of 10x MEM.
Vortex the mixture for 5 sec prior to use, keeping it on ice and storing at 4 °C when not in immediate use.
Place a 12 well plate in -20 °C for 10 min.
Place a 20 ml syringe in -20 °C for 10 min.
Spray all tubes and well plates to be used with 70% ethanol.
Let the sprayed items dry for sterilization.
Place a 20 ml syringe on ice to cool.
Open stainless steel molds to release BSA rubber under PCR hood.
Cut exhaust channels of the BSA rubber mold using a scalpel.
Open sterile collagen tubes and add 1 ml HEPES-MEM solution.
Thoroughly mix collagen and buffer solution with a sterile spatula.
Close and vortex the mixed hydrogel quickly.
Transfer the mixed hydrogel to a cold 20 ml syringe.
Hold BSA Rubber inside of the well using one hand.
Dispense half of the collagen hydrogel solution onto the bottom of the well using the other hand.
Ensure that the rubber inflow and outflow ends are touching the sides of the well with sterile tweezers.
Pour collagen solution on top until the BSA rubber is completely covered.
Ensure there are no bubbles, especially near the ends of the rubber.
Place the cover on the well.
Wrap Parafilm around the circumference of the well.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Turn on the PCR UV light.
UV crosslink the hydrogel using a UV crosslinker apparatus set to irradiate with 630,000 µJ/cm² energy.
Remove the gels from the incubator and spray hands with ethanol.
Inside the chamber, quickly remove the lid of the well plate.
Close the chamber and UV crosslink the hydrogels by selecting an energy setting of 630,000 µJ/cm².
After crosslinking, turn off the UV light on the PCR hood.
Spray hands with ethanol and open the chamber, placing the lid back onto the well plate quickly.
Move the well plate to the PCR hood.
Using a sterile spatula, gently loosen and remove the gel from the well plate.
Flip the gels under the hood to crosslink the bottom of the hydrogel.
Repeat steps involving UV crosslinking and handling with ethanol as needed.
Turn on the UV light for 20-30 minutes to sterilize the tissue culture hood.
Make a 0.25% trypsin solution pH 7.8.
Add 0.0376 g of trypsin to 15 ml of water in a 50 ml conical tube.
Adjust the pH to 7.8 by adding small amounts (2-5 µl) of 1 M NaCl.
Place the solution in a 20 ml syringe and cap with a 0.20 µm syringe filter.
Press the plunger to expel liquid through the filter and collect the sterile solution in a new tube.
Turn on the water bath and set the temperature to 30 °C.
Spray ethanol on all tubes and materials that will be used in the hood.
Transfer collagen hydrogel under the hood and place it in a separate conical tube.
Add around 3-5 ml of 0.25% trypsin solution with pH 7.8 to each tube.
Seal the tubes with Parafilm and vortex lightly for approximately 1 min.
Place the sealed tubes in the 30 °C water bath for 15-24 hr.
Lightly vortex the gels frequently while in the water bath until BSA rubber is digested or removed from the hydrogel.
Turn on the PCR hood UV light for 20-30 min.
Prepare Moscona solution by combining potassium chloride (KCl, 28.6 mM), sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3, 11.9 mM), glucose (9.4 mM), and sodium dihydrogen phosphate (NaH2PO4, 0.08 mM) in water.
Adjust the pH to 7.4 using 1 M NaOH or 12 M HCl solution.
Place the prepared Moscona solution in a 20 ml syringe.
Sterilize the solution by passing it through a 0.20 µm syringe filter.
Spray all equipment with ethanol and allow it to dry before use.
Transfer 5-10 ml of sterile Moscona solution to a new 50 ml conical tube.
Add collagen hydrogel to the conical tube containing the enzyme solution, ensuring complete coverage.
Incubate the mixture in a shaker at 4 °C for 30 minutes.
Aspirate the Moscona solution and repeat the incubation step twice more with fresh sterile Moscona solution.
Store the treated collagen hydrogel at 4 °C.
